topicName: Active Directory Attacks (Kerberoasting, BloodHound, Golden Ticket)
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Advanced Active Directory Attacks: Kerberoasting, BloodHound, and Golden Tickets"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Active Directory (AD) is the backbone of identity and access management in most enterprise networks. When performing ethical hacking or red team assessments, mastering AD enumeration and exploitation is critical. This tutorial covers three foundational AD attack vectors: Kerberoasting, BloodHound path analysis, and Golden Ticket generation."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Kerberoasting"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Kerberoasting targets Service Principal Names (SPNs). Any domain user can request a Ticket Granting Service (TGS) ticket for any service associated with an SPN. Because these tickets are encrypted with the password hash of the service account, an attacker can extract them from memory and offline-brute-force them."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Prerequisites: Valid domain user credentials."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Impact: Plaintext password recovery for service accounts (often SQL, IIS, etc.)."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"GetUserSPNs.py corp.local/john.doe:Password123 -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 -request"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. BloodHound and Attack Path Analysis"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"BloodHound uses graph theory to reveal the hidden and often unintended relationships within an Active Directory environment. By mapping ACLs, group memberships, and sessions, it identifies the shortest path to Domain Admin privileges."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 1: Execute the BloodHound collector (SharpHound) on a compromised machine."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 2: Import the resulting JSON files into the BloodHound GUI."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 3: Run pre-built queries such as 'Find all Domain Admins' or 'Shortest Path from Domain Users to Domain Admin'."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"SharpHound.exe -CollectionMethod All"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Golden Ticket Attack"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Golden Ticket attack is a post-exploitation technique where an attacker who has gained Domain Administrator privileges (specifically the NTLM hash of the krbtgt account) crafts their own Kerberos Ticket Granting Ticket (TGT). This grants perpetual, stealthy access to any resource in the domain, bypassing standard authentication controls."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Prerequisites: Domain Admin access, krbtgt account NTLM hash, Domain SID."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"mimikatz.exe \"kerberos::golden /domain:corp.local /sid:S-1-5-21-123456789-987654321-1122334455 /krbtgt:abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890 /user:HackerAdmin /ptt\""},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Remediation and Defense"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"To defend against these vectors, organizations must implement strong password policies for service accounts (15+ characters), utilize Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA) which automatically manage passwords, monitor for abnormal TGS request volumes (Event ID 4769), and regularly audit permissions using BloodHound defensively to fix dangerous ACLs."}]
